{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2017–18 |team=New Mexico State Aggies |image=New Mexico State Aggies wordmark.svg |image_size=250 |conference=Western Athletic Conference |division= |short_conf=WAC |record=28–6 |conf_record=12–2 |CoachRank= |APRank= |head_coach=[[Chris Jans]] |hc_year = 1st |asst_coach1=Lou Gudino |asst_coach2=David Anwar |asst_coach3=Jeff Mailhot |asst_coach4= |stadium=[[Pan American Center]] |champion=WAC regular season and [[2018 WAC men's basketball tournament|tournament]] champions |bowl=[[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = First Round }} {{2017–18 WAC men's basketball standings}} The '''2017–18 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team''' represented [[New Mexico State University]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Aggies, led by first-year head coach [[Chris Jans]], played their home games at the [[Pan American Center]] in [[Las Cruces, New Mexico]] as members of the [[Western Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 28–6, 12–2 in WAC play to win the WAC regular season championship. In the [[2018 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]], they defeated [[2017–18 Chicago State Cougars men's basketball team|Chicago State]], [[2017–18 Seattle Redhawks men's basketball team|Seattle]], and [[2017–18 Grand Canyon Antelopes men's basketball team|Grand Canyon]] to become WAC Tournament champions. They received the WAC's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2017–18 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]]. == Previous season == The [[2016–17 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team|Aggies]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 28–6, 11–3 in WAC play to finish in a tie for second place. They defeated [[2016–17 Chicago State Cougars men's basketball team|Chicago State]], [[2016–17 UMKC Kangaroos men's basketball team|UMKC]], and [[2016–17 Cal State Bakersfield Roadrunners men's basketball team|Cal State Bakersfield]] to win the [[2017 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]]. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2016–17 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]]. On April 11, 2017, head coach [[Paul Weir (basketball)|Paul Weir]] resigned to become the head coach at [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]].{{cite web |author= Glen Rosales, The Associated Press |url= https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2017-04-11/college-basketball-new-mexico-hires-nmsus-paul-weir-head |title= College basketball: New Mexico hires NMSU's Paul Weir as head coach |website= NCAA.com |date= 2017-04-11 |accessdate= 2017-12-11}} On April 17, the school hired [[Chris Jans]] as head coach.{{Cite news |url= http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/new-mexico-state-hires-wichita-state-assistant-chris-jans-to-replace-paul-weir/ |title= New Mexico State hires Wichita State assistant Chris Jans to replace Paul Weir |work= CBSSports.com |access-date= 2017-06-28 |language= en}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- !
